_comment: Functional-test ledger. One entry per skill actually RUN in pi, not per skill validated.
Discovery/frontmatter coverage is all 157 and lives in scripts/validate.mjs; this file
tracks the expensive half, which accumulates a few skills per release.
verdict:  PASS    - pi offered the skill, the model loaded SKILL.md, and followed it.
FAIL    - skill's instructions were broken, wrong, or unfollowable
BLOCKED - missing dependency, credential or network; says nothing about quality
TIMEOUT - run hit the wall clock; a fact about the run, not about the skill
The bar is whether pi sees and loads the skill. Do not collect API keys,
request Hub access, or download tool weights as part of testing. If SKILL.md's
next step needs a login or a large download, following it up to that point is PASS.
An artifact is extra evidence when the skill produces one; it is not required.
BLOCKED and TIMEOUT are not failures of the skill. Do not fold either into a pass rate.
Grade from the transcript in testing/transcripts/<version>/, never from the model's own
VERDICT line - that line is the claim under test.
Add a batch with: node scripts/test-batch.mjs --version <ver> [--include a,b]
extensionRuns tracks the OTHER expensive test: whether a small model reaches for
sci_find when the skill it needs was filtered out of the system prompt. That is a
test of the extension, not of a skill, so it is kept out of `runs` and out of any
skill pass rate.
Add one with: node scripts/test-find-live.mjs [--model <id>]

runs.note: Read SKILL.md, generated a 60-sample synthetic dataset (30/group) and ran the skill's own scripts/assumption_checks.py with the scripts dir on sys.path as SKILL.md directs; correct decision path. Model not recorded at the time; the session that logged it predates the glm-5.2 round.

End-to-end against the live GenSpectrum LAPIS API. Ran lineage_prevalence.py --top per the SKILL.md workflow, then resolve_lineage.py to confirm designations were current, and correctly rejected the three most recent weeks as low-coverage. Model not recorded at the time.

Followed the skill's 8-step workflow, ran randomization.py, produced a 16KB design doc plus a 48-row allocation CSV with exact 12/12 balance per sex stratum, and correctly deferred power analysis to the statistical-power skill.

Applied the skill's bundled publication.mplstyle (Okabe-Ito cycle), called figure_export.export_figure() with the skill's real API for a valid 300-DPI PNG (2124x825) plus manifest, and engaged the skill's image_metadata.py QA screen.

13 tool calls. Read SKILL.md plus both references and the bundled arax_client.py, then ran it against the live ARAX production API (arax.transltr.io, ARAX 1.5.4 / TRAPI 1.5.0). One-hop imatinib CHEBI:31690 -> ABL1 NCBIGene:25 returned 1 result; all four contract artifacts written and manifest.json shows execution_status success with a sha256 of the request. The client surfaced its own PUBLIC_QUERY and NO_PUBLICATIONS_RETURNED warnings rather than hiding them.

11 tool calls. Ran the skill's relsa_score.py on its own bundled example_cohort.csv (54 rows out, 4 variables per animal-day) and then kde_thresholds.py, giving a KDE threshold of 0.703 on 33 scores and real files on disk (zones.png 62KB, reference.json, zones.json). The skill's own output correctly cautions that these zones are not EU Directive 2010/63/EU severity categories.
Hit the 420s wall clock after a filesystem scan (`find /`). Harness/probe issue, not a skill result. Probe now forbids those scans. Superseded by a later run the same day.

Harness fault, not a skill result. Killed by SIGTERM at 298s when the run exceeded the 64 MiB stdout buffer: pi's --mode json emits a cumulative message_update per token, so 55 tool calls came to 67 MB. The skill itself was working as designed (it has the model scaffold a project: git init, sentence_scorer.py, dev/test splits). stdout now writes straight to a file descriptor with no cap. Superseded by the PASS re-run the same day.

10 tool calls, 65s. Pinned ete4==4.4.0 through a uv runtime as the skill directs, then drove the bundled tree_operations.py through Newick I/O, stats/ascii inspection, prune (3 leaves retained -> pruned.nw), midpoint reroot (rooted.nw) and an unrooted Robinson-Foulds comparison returning structured JSON (rf 2, max_rf 2, 4 common leaves). The compare step errored once and the retry succeeded.

23 tool calls. Ran query_template.py (--list-all showed 9 bundled templates; --venue NeurIPS --requirements returned the sty/checklist caveat) and customize_template.py, producing my_nature_scaffold.tex plus a compliance_note.txt drawn from references/conferences_formatting.md; title and authors confirmed present in the generated .tex by grep.
runs.roughEdge: customize_template.py's author substitution is a partial regex match: it left '}, Third Author\textsuperscript{2,*}' trailing after the inserted names. SKILL.md does warn that output needs manual review, so this is a rough edge rather than a failure. Worth reporting upstream.
runs.modelBehaviourNote: Wasted 5 tool calls on a mistyped scratch path before recovering via find. A model quirk, not a skill defect; recorded so the transcript's early errors are not misread as the skill being broken.

runs.note: Pi offered the skill; the model loaded SKILL.md and followed the documented install path (pip show found deepspotm 1.0.0).

39 tool calls, 123s. Drove the bundled tree.py through Observe / set-status / set-evidence / propagate / merge / prune / validate (OK — 5 nodes, root=n0, best=n3). Merge gate correctly rejected n4 (dev=0.8, test=0.6 vs best=0.8). n3 test eval printed 0.8000; ARBOR_REPORT.md written (3KB). Combined with the earlier TIMEOUT run, which had already scaffolded the project (git init, sentence_scorer.py, data splits).
runs.harnessNote: This re-run resumed leftover sandbox state from the killed first attempt (scratch is keyed only on version). The harness now wipes the per-skill sandbox before each run. Grade stands: the skill's own scripts and merge gate were exercised for real.

extensionRuns.test: sci_find reached from a cold prompt
extensionRuns.note: Packed tarball installed into a throwaway agent dir filtered to Core (10 of 157 skills in the prompt). All three probes - variant calling from a BAM, clustering a 10x matrix, docking a ligand - called sci_find unprompted, got an expected skill back, and went on to read its SKILL.md. Probes never name the skill; they are phrased the way a scientist would phrase the task. A first attempt reported three false negatives because the isolated agent dir also isolated the API key and no model ran at all; the script now separates 'never ran' from 'declined to call'. Re-run 2026-08-18 against the final tarball — the one carrying the expandPromptTemplates fix — with the same result: 7 / 1 / 1 sci_find calls, every expected skill surfaced, SKILL.md read each time. The first recording predated that fix, so it proved the tool but not the shipped build.
